title.narrative: FAIR4ALL Regional Value Chains in Asia

description.narrative: The Power of Voices Partnership (PvP) is an influencing programme with the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The programme FAIR for ALL led by Oxfam Novib is five year long initiative implemented jointly with consortium members Huairou Commission, SOMO and Third World Network-Africa (TWN-Africa) aimed at supporting and collaborating with people’s rightful demands towards companies, governments and multilateral organizations for economic, social and environmental justice, promoting global trade and value-chains that are fair for all. The main focus of the FAIR for ALL programme proposal is to support and strengthen CSOs to play their diverse roles; as educators, mobilizers, creators and watchdogs to make trade and value chains FAIR for ALL. In Asia, FAIR for ALL programme aims at a stronger regional movement of CSOs, small producers, workers and women create spaces, mobilize citizens and act together with progressive governments and private sector towards inclusive and sustainable value chains inAsia that respect human rights and the environment, promote women’s economic empowerment. The Asia FAIR for ALL programme will be implemented by Oxfam in Asia and partners, aiming to: 1)Convening and capacity building for a more responsible private andfinancial sector: we work with all five PVP countries in Asia on research and campaigning capacity building and expanding civic space through alliances/networking. 2) Engagement with the ASEAN and member states: we will work with all four ASEAN membersstates who are part of PvP on fiscal governance and ASEAN inclusive business framework; 3) contributing to shifting the terms of debate (PW 1,2,3,4)- this will lead- work with all countries to showcase their alternate business models at regional level. These objectives will be achieved by Convene and support CSOs, workers, women’s rights organizations and producers to raise their collective voices against violations of human rights, women’s right andlabour rights; Capacity strengthening of CSOs in research, public campaigning and advocacy for inclusive and sustainable value chains and against shrinking civic space; promoting fair fiscal governance and progressive spending to ASEAN, its member states, and other South Asian governments. Additionally, through research and alliance building, develop thought leadership on alternative, inclusive business models, and raising awareness of and engage with the Asian public and sensitize the media to create a public constituency asking for inclusive and sustainable value chains and strong government regulations to protect human rights and the environment. To achieve main objectives of the programme in Asia, Oxfam will collaborate with Tax and Fiscal Justice Network Asia (TAFJA); SAAPE; Convening a bottom up built agribusiness network-To convene a network of agriculture workers, small producers, women rights organization and other workers affected by unfair practices of value chains led by women rights organization to articulate and amplify voices for fair value chains; finally we will work with a research partner.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam International was formed in 1995 by a group of independent non-governmental organizations. Their aim was to work together forgreater impact on the international stage to reduce poverty and injustice. The name "Oxfam" comes from the Oxford Committee for Famine Relief, founded in Britain in 1942. The group campaigned for food supplies to be sent through an allied naval blockade to starving women and children in enemy-occupied Greece during the Second World War. As well as becoming a world leader in the delivery of emergency relief, Oxfam International implements long-term development programs in vulnerable communities. We are also part of a global movement, campaigning with others, for instance, to end unfair trade rules, demand better health and education services for all, and to combat climate change. Today, there are 19 member organizations of the Oxfam International confederation. They are based in: Australia, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Great Britain, Hong Kong, Ireland, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, The Netherlands, New Zealand, Quebec, South Africa, Spain and the United States. The Oxfam International Secretariat is based in Oxford, UK. The Secretariat runs advocacy offices in Addis Ababa, Brussels, Geneva, New York and Washington DC.

The Parliamentarian Interaction Programme on UN Tax Convention and Tax Justice in the Context of Nepal, held on 25 November 2024, in Kathmandu, Nepal brought together policymakers, tax experts, and civil society representatives to discuss Nepal’s role inglobal tax governance. Organized by APMDD, LDC Watch, SAAPE, and RRN, the event emphasized the significance of the UN Tax Convention in ensuring a fair international tax system, addressing illicit financial flows, and promoting progressive taxation. Speakers, including Lidy Nacpil, Dr. Dilli Raj Khanal, Bidhyadhar Malik and various parliamentarians, underscored the need for tax reforms, wealth taxation, and stronger domestic resource mobilization to bridge inequality and finance sustainable development. Discussions also covered the digital economy, tax evasion, and Nepal’s engagement in global tax reforms. The event concluded with a call for policy actions to strengthen Nepal’s tax system and enhance its position in international tax negotiations. comment.narrative: "[PRAKARSA] Research titled ""Fiscal Incentives and Human Rights in ASEAN Fishery Industry: Assessment of the Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) Implementation,"" Prakarsa explores the interplay between economic incentives, human rights, and the fishery industry within the ASEAN region. The research focuses on assessing the implementation of Human Rights Due Diligence, examining how fiscal policies impact human rights conditions for individuals involved in the fishery sector. This work aims to provide insights into the complex relationship between fiscal measures, business practices, and the well-being of those working in the ASEAN fishery industry. During research work in the 3rd year, PRAKARSA took a multi-sector approach and succeeded in expanding itsnetwork through collaboration with various CSOs at both national and regional levels, as well as holding targeted hearings and discussions with governments such as the Ministry of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, the Ministry of Finance through the FiscalPolicy Agency, Ministry of Law and Human Rights, and The Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency. A series of research processes that begin with multi-party discussions to formulate research concept notes; followed by data collection, both secondary data and primary data using the IDI process carried out in the field; external review process to discuss research findings and data analysis with several parties such as academics, practitioners and CSOs."

"1) Submission of Demand Letter to the Minister of Plantation and Community Infrastructure (Sri Lanka) on Tea Workers’ and Smallholders’ Rights 2) LDC Watch Global Coordinator's participation in ""Fair, Inclusive, and Anti-Racist Economies to Leave NoOne Behind"" organised by the Governments of Brasil and South Africa along with C20 Brasil, ABONG, UN Women, and other civil society organisations, held in the UN Headquarter on the side line of the Summit of The Future (SOTF).3) Intervention by LDC Watch Global Coordinator on behalf of the Civil Society Financing for Development Mechanism at the United Nations Intersessional Multi-Stakeholder Hearing in preparation for the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4), held in New York on 28 October 2024.4) Oxfam in Asia's continued support and participation to the 7th ASEAN Inclusive Business (IB) Forum on 23 – 24 September 2024 in Vientiane under Lao PDR’s ASEAN chairmanship, with the focused theme on IB accreditation. "[SAAPE] Federation of Agriculture and Plantation Workers Union of Nepal (FAPWUN) (an affiliate of GEFONT), Nepal Tea Garden Workers Union (NTGWU) (an affiliate of Nepal Trade Union Congress), and All Nepal Tea Workers Union (an affiliate of All Nepal Trade Union Federation) conducted a joint struggle (sit-ins and protests) in Jhapa district of Nepal from 24 July to 03 September 2023, ultimately leading to increase in minimum wage, private sectors' commitment to implement the increased minimum wage in the tea estates, and inclusion of regular plantations workers in state announced social security schemes.*SAAPE counts as 2: One is a sit-in protest and one is a public demonstration that took place between 24 July and 3 September, when the demands ultimately got addressed by the State. Earlier, they announced a series of protest programs to press their demands. [PRAKARSA] The effort by PRAKARSA on the side event of the 6th ASEAN Inclusive Business Summit 2023, Bali, from 2.1.1.In 2022, when the 5th IB Summit was held in Cambodia, the space was more opened. Oxfam had the opportunity to engage in the official programme with John, Oxfam Asia Regional Director, delivering speech and Oxfam in Cambodia facilitating one of the session. In 2023, the situation was different in Bali and it was less opened. The partner / local network could not be part of the formal programme so the CSOs had to go with a parallel / side event. However, PKS engaged a lot with the responsible ministry of Indonesia and some of the key government officials attended the side event."

description.narrative: Strengthened civil society works in people-led coalitions that hold private-sector actors to account.
2.2.1 Cases of Influential stakeholders endorsing communities in protecting their rights in trade and/or value chains

comment.narrative: "[SAAPE] #1 - Honorable Member of the Federal Parliament of Nepal Bijula Rajyamajhi, who is also the member of the Agriculture, Cooperative and Natural Resource Parliamentary Committee, was one of the attendees of the policy dialogue event held on tea sector in Nepal on 25 September 2023. She reminded the responsibility of the private sector and respect the labour of plantation workers and further expressed her commitment to present the Tea Declaration, released during the event, in the Agriculture, Cooperative and Natural Resource Parliamentary Committee and also place the problems/issues of tea sector as an agenda in one of the Committee meetings.#2 - On receipt of the 28-point Tea Declaration (under 2.1.1), Dr. Bishnu Prasad Bhattarai, the Executive Director of NTCDB thanked the deputation for the Declaration, which he said would act as a “guidance” or “advisory” document for the Board. He further appreciated the participation of civil society in such crucial development issue. He expressed his commitment to implement all the 28 points stated in the Declaration."

description.narrative: 2.2.5 Cases of increased or protected civic space for coalitions to hold private and financial sector to account for respecting Human Rights in their value chain

comment.narrative: 1) Regional Convergence of Tea Plantation Workers – Organized by SAAPE; brought together workers, trade unions, women’s groups, peasants, and human rights advocates from across South Asia. Issued the Kathmandu Declaration calling for social security and a living wage. Formed the South Asia Tea Plantation Workers’ Coalition to coordinate rights advocacy. 2) Regional Convergence of Tea Smallholders – Co-organized by SAAPE and SAPC; addressed inequalities in agriculture, market exploitation, land rights, and climate vulnerability. Emphasized cooperative-led initiatives, regional collaboration, and equitable policies. Established a regional tea smallholders’ working group for future advocacy. 3) SAAPE Staff Capacity-Building – Jointly organized by LDC Watch and SAAPE (hosted by RRN) to strengthen staff capacity on shrinking civic space, climate change, and economic pressures. Covered rural revitalization, leadership, advocacy, and networking, resulting in actionable strategies focused on collaboration and climate connectivity. 4) Asia Inclusive & Responsible Business Forum – Convened by Oxfam in Asia and partners; engaged 160+ participants from 90+ organizations including corporations, SMEs, banks, policymakers, and civil society. Explored fair wages, gender equality, climate-resilient supply chains, HRDD, sustainability, and circular economy through interactive sessions. 5) Revival of Oxfam’s Asia Private Sector Working Group (PSWG) – Aligned on three priorities: Corporate Accountability & HRDD, SME Engagement, and Gender & Unpaid Care Work. Formed dedicated teams and focal points with a 12‑month work plan to strengthen coordination, outreach, and funding prospects.

Asia Inclusive and responsible business forum provided protected civic space for holding a public discussion around making businesses more inclusive and human centric. It was an opportunity for civil society to listen to the practices private sector has been implementing and share their experiences with them and propose ideas and suggestions reflecting the ground realities and human needs, as well as, express CSOs concerns to both the private sector and International Organisations together with Diplomatic representatives who were present at the forum.

description.narrative: CSOs demonstrating increased expertise in holding private/financial sector actors to account

comment.narrative: Bangladesh Nari Pragoti Sangha and Progressive Plantation Workers; Union participated in the protest held in Bangladesh on the minimum wage issue. The representatives from these organizations were continuously engaged with the SAAPE during discussions and meetings on the issues of tea sector. And continued the struggle by taking part in the process of the protest. Similarly, Pakistan Fisherfolk Forum and National Fisheries Solidarity Organization have also been organising campaigns for seafood workers' welfare. In Sri Lanka, Upcountry social research forum conducted a policy dialogue with the private sector companies of Tea sector. All these organisations had attended the regional capacity-building event held on the issue of fair value chain in Kathmandu, Nepal.

[SAAPE] (1) Federation of Agriculture and Plantation Workers Union of Nepal (FAPWUN) (an affiliate of GEFONT), (2) Nepal Tea Garden Workers Union (NTGWU) (an affiliate of Nepal Trade Union Congress), and (3) All Nepal Tea Workers Union (an affiliate of All Nepal Trade Union Federation) conducted a joint struggle (sit-ins and protests) in Jhapa district of Nepal against the privately held tea estates demanding wage increment, labour registry, and inclusion in the government launched social security schemes in Nepal. The protest started on 24 July 2023 and ended on 03 September 2023 with an agreement with the Nepal Tea Producers' Association (the tea estates' coalition), the decisions being that the plantation workers will be provided with increased minimum wage (NPR 600/day) and the permanent workers will be included under the government-launched contribution-based social security scheme.

description.narrative: Men mobilized in southern project countries around protecting communities' rights in trade and/or value chains

comment.narrative: "1) Mobilization of the Tea Sector Union to Implement Workers’ Rights and Benefits (W 47, M 23)LDC Watch/ SAAPE in collaboration with Tea and Coffee Workers' Union Nepal organised the national consultation of tea plantation workers on 11 March 2025 in Jhapa, Nepal. The demands of the workers, based on the consultation, were submitted to the Chief Minister of Koshi province Honourable Hikmat Karki on 30 March 2025. 2) Plantation Sector: Challenges and Solutions (W 14, M 37)Human Development Organization (HDO), Up-Country Social Research Centre, National Fisheries Solidarity Movement (NAFSO) and Women’s Development Innovators (WDI), together with LDC Watch and SAAPE, organised an event “Plantation Sector: Challenges and Solutions” in Hatton, Sri Lanka on 31 March 2025. The plantation workers’ challenges and recommendations stated during the event will be used to finalise the demand document to be submitted to the relevant government authority later. Participants included parliamentarians, political party members, members of the local government authorities, former ministry secretary, trade unionists, civil society activists, women leaders, academics, professionals, journalists, researchers, estate workers, religious heads and NGO personnel."

"Public mobilisation of workers on the occasion of International Worker's Day (1 May 2023)[SAAPE] Demanding sustainable solutions to the concerns of plantation workers in Nepal, Federation of Agriculture and Plantation Workers Union of Nepal (FAPWUN) (an affiliate of GEFONT, a SAAPE member), held a public rally in Jhapa (Koshi province, Nepal) on the occasion of International Workers’ Day on 1 May 2023. Men and women, who participated in the public rally, chanted the slogans: Our rights are being curtailed! Let’s get organised, trained, and mobilized! Let’s intervene for our rights!Subsequent to the May Day event, a discussion was held among the representatives from the Federation of Agriculture and Plantation Workers Union of Nepal (FAPWUN) (an affiliate of GEFONT), Nepal Tea Garden Workers Union (NTGWU) (an affiliate of Nepal Trade Union Congress), and All Nepal Tea Workers Union (an affiliate of All Nepal Trade Union Federation) on the contents of the demand letter addressed to the Regional Office ofNational Tea and Coffee Development Board (NTCDB) urging the Tea Board to take steps towards urgently addressing the issues of establishing a uniform minimum wage for tea and other sectors, revising wage on a scientific basis, provisioning of social protection facilities to both formal and informal workers in the tea sector, and registration of tea workers at the local level. Finally, the demand letter, agreed by all three major trade unions working on the tea sector in Nepal was submitted to the ActingRegional Director of the National Tea and Coffee Development Board, Jhapa."
